core_obligations: Reduce to injective sheaves (proof lines 6091-6095): represent the given complex by a K-injective complex with injective terms, so that it suffices to treat a single injective abelian sheaf.

Exactness at the first arrow (proof lines 6101-6104): the injectivity follows because the pushout condition makes the map from the coproduct of the two pushforwards to the third surjective after sheafification, so the two arrows form a covering.

Exactness at the last arrow (proof lines 6105-6110): surjectivity follows from the injectivity of the sheaf and the injectivity of the corresponding map of free sheaves, the values being described as homomorphism groups.

Exactness in the middle (proof lines 6113-6122): two sections agreeing on the fourth object define a map from the sheafified coproduct which factors through the sheafified pushout by hypothesis, and the pushout condition produces a unique section over the first object restricting to them.
proof_roadmap: Replace the complex by a K-injective complex of injective sheaves to reduce to a single injective sheaf.
Show the displayed sequence is exact on the left using the pushout condition.
Show exactness on the right using injectivity, and exactness in the middle by factoring a map through the pushout.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that when a commutative square has the property that the sheafification of the coproduct of two of its objects is the third and one leg is injective, the construction attached to the square yields a distinguished triangle of global section complexes, functorially in the complex (statement lines 6073-6089). The proof is a complete reduction to sheaves and a hand verification of exactness: a K-injective representative with injective terms reduces the assertion to a single injective sheaf (proof lines 6091-6095); exactness at the first arrow is read off from the pushout condition (proof lines 6101-6104); exactness at the last arrow uses injectivity and the description of sections as homomorphisms from a sheafified free sheaf (proof lines 6105-6110); and exactness in the middle is proved by factoring a map through the pushout and producing a unique amalgamation (proof lines 6113-6122). The non-formal content is the three exactness verifications. The claim is H2: a reduction followed by a written-out case analysis.
